items.title: George Avakian interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 21, 1998
items.q: I said, 'No, we’re just friends, I came over to see how you were, I heard you weren’t feeling well.'

ctx.x: Yeah, the “dark prince” business yeah. Well it worked very well for him. But he developed it really over a period of time. And because he was a kind of a lonesome person and he was always ailing, you know there was always something wrong with Miles. He had problems with his bones, he had eventually diabetes, he had everything it seems. And when he wasn’t doing too much he would occasionally call up and say hey come on over to the house and hang out. And he had nothing particularly to talk about but he just…

George, what do you want?” I said, “What do you mean what do I want?” “Well does Ar want me to do a movie soundtrack for him or something?” I said, “No, no, no.” Well he said, “Well I thought you wanted me for something.” I said, “No, we’re just friends, I came over to see how you were, I heard you weren’t feeling well.” And it took him a little while to realize that that was the only reason that I’d called him up.
